Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co Announces Major Investment to Boost Capacity

Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co has unveiled plans for a significant investment aimed at expanding its refining capacity, reinforcing its position as a cornerstone of the Kingdom’s energy sector. The move, announced at a press briefing in Amman on Sunday, comes as part of the company’s ongoing strategy to meet rising domestic demand for petroleum products and support Jordan’s economic development.

The planned expansion, valued at over $600 million according to company sources, will focus on upgrading processing units and increasing daily output by approximately 20%. The project is expected to create hundreds of jobs throughout its construction phase and generate sustained employment once operational.

Eng. Ahmad Al-Khatib, CEO of Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co, highlighted the importance of the investment for the national economy. “Our expansion will not only enhance supply stability but also reduce reliance on imported fuels,” Al-Khatib said. “This is a vital step towards energy security and self-sufficiency for Jordan.”

Industry analysts welcomed the announcement, noting that increased refining capacity could help moderate fuel prices and strengthen Jordan’s energy independence. Samira Haddad, an energy sector analyst at Amman-based consultancy PetraEnergy, commented, “This investment is a timely response to growing consumption and will position Jordan as a more resilient player in the regional energy market.”

The Jordanian Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources voiced support for the initiative, emphasizing its alignment with national development goals. The ministry stated that the expansion is expected to contribute to Jordan’s GDP and enhance the competitiveness of local industries.

Construction is scheduled to begin later this year, with completion projected within 36 months. Local suppliers and engineering firms, including Al-Rashid Engineering, are set to participate in the project, further stimulating economic activity in the region.
